cameron: Heads-up — noticed a p99 tail spike in decode after yesterday's kernel selector change. prefill p95 roughly stable, but decode p99 went from ~85ms -> ~220ms on rtx-pool :eyes:

jia: I saw that in the perf dashboard. looks correlated with higher microbatch sizes in the rollout (we bumped max_microbatch from 16 -> 32). could be kernel fallback on long sequences or a slow kernel chosen for certain seq len distribution.

olivia: Can we get a flamegraph or a quick trace? even a short aggregated profile should tell whether slow path is matmul/kernel or kv/cache overhead.

cameron: Attached the short profile export from yesterday's spike window (snip):
```
TRACE_SUMMARY decode_total: 220ms (p99)
  kernel_select: 6ms
  kernel_exec: 180ms  # gemm_quant_v2 slowpath
  kv_cache_lookup: 18ms
  io/serialization: 10ms
```

remy: The kv numbers are higher than usual but not dominant for the p99. kernel_exec dominating. gemm_quant_v2 slowpath is the suspect — that's the kernel we land on when the selector sees >512 tokens or when a quant condition fails. We rolled a small selector tweak yesterday to prefer a new 'packed-gemm' kernel for medium batches; maybe its heuristic misfires at certain microbatch shapes.

jia: Repro plan: 1) reproduce with microbatch=32 and seq=600 2) run with --kernel-telemetry to log selected kernel per request 3) try forcing selector to old heuristic to compare. I'll kick that off now.

sre: FYI this caused a brief alert on the prod latency watch but fell back to canary capacity. No user-facing errors. Still want to fix since cost and p99 matters.

perf-ci-bot: perf trace uploaded -> https://perf.ci/runs/2147654321/trace.html :white_check_mark:

olivia: Quick observation from the trace: when microbatch_size is high, the selector's cost model multiplies by batch_size but misses that the new kernel's setup latency scales worse with uneven sequence lengths (padding math). Effectively the selector underestimates per-token cost, so it picks packed-gemm which has a heavier setup for variable-length.

remy: That matches local repro: uniform short sequences still prefer fast_fp16, but mixed seqs (one long, many short) end up in packed-gemm and pay the setup for the long one. Also KV warmup: splitpoint change last week delayed prefix warming for requests that start with streaming chunks, increasing KV miss rate by ~25% for some routes. Combined effect explains tail.

cameron: Two immediate mitigations proposed:
- tighten selector heuristic: penalize kernels with O(batch * setup) if seq_len variance > threshold
- lower max_microbatch default from 32 -> 20 for rtx-pool until selector fix
- re-enable aggressive KV prefetch for splitpoint=stream-start flows

jia: I ran the forced-selector experiment. Results: forcing old heuristic drops decode p99 from 220 -> 95ms in the repro window. microbatch=32 + forced_old_selector yields decode p99 ~98ms. So selector change is primary.

olivia: Good signal. For longer term, we should add a small estimator that computes expected setup cost: sample sequence length distribution from the microbatch and compute "effective_setup = median_setup * (1 + var_norm)" and add that to kernel score. Should be cheap and avoid regressions.

remy: On KV side I pushed a tiny change to bump prefetch window for streaming splitpoint when kv_cache_miss_rate > 15%. Will monitor.

cameron: Action items:
- jia: patch to rollback the selector heuristic or add a quick safety cap (due EOD)
- olivia: prototype variance-aware cost estimator (PR draft)
- remy: monitor KV miss after prefetch bump, report delta in 24h
- sre: hold latency alerts to pass/cooldown while we mitigate (opt-in)

jia: I'm opening the rollback PR now with a simple gate: if seq_len_variance > 0.3 then prefer fallback kernel. link -> https://git/repo/pull/8421 :wrench:

perf-ci-bot: CI perf job queued for PR 8421 (compare baseline vs rollback).

olivia: Also adding a small perf test matrix: microbatch sizes [8,16,24,32], seq patterns [uniform short, one-long-many-short, even-long] so we can produce a heatmap. Will attach results to the PR.

remy: quick note: keep an eye on cost per-token when forcing older kernel — sometimes p99 improves but unit cost jumps. we need cost vs latency tradeoff in the PR description.

cameron: Agreed. We care about latency SLOs first here, but any mitigation must include delta in p95/p99 and token cost.

jia: Rolling the safety cap to canary now (5% traffic). will update with canary numbers in ~30m. :thumbsup:

sre: Thanks — will mute the noisy channel alerts and follow the canary.

cameron: If canary looks good, we promote and follow up with variance estimator in next sprint. thanks everyone. :rocket:
